shared.is: the scale rules every place keeps
rules: One object per model, reading as what it does, clean up close.
Modules and moving parts are built in code.
If it is not boxed on this scene's kept plan, it is not in the room.
A model is scaled uniformly to its row's size and nothing else; a wrong one is retaken from a better picture.
No shared kit of parts: a prop belongs to one place; two places share a model only when the owner picks that on page B.

style.text: A lived-in industrial working station crossed with a dense high-tech cockpit. The structure is worn and patched: bolted metal panels, exposed pipes and valves, hand wheels, tool boards, scuffed deck plates and taped repairs, a base that has been worked hard for years. The work places are dense with technology: screens, readouts, switches, labelled breakers and neat cable runs at every console, desk and rack. Lit by hard work lamps over the structure and by the screens at the work places, with real shadow between. The habitat's mix leans lived-in industrial: worn grey bolted panels, pipes and hand wheels high on the walls, a scuffed deck; the crew's own corners are calmer: pale panelled sleep pods with their own reading lamps and small screens, a clean pale hygiene cubicle and medical corner (clean institutional), a round light ring over the mess table at the room's middle.
style.from: the base theme (shared.theme) and the habitat's picked concept K03 (concepts-world1/habitat)
style.picked: 2026-10-07, the coordinator's pick for the owner (asleep): the picked concept's mix within the base theme

was.text: Inside a small Chinese state outpost on the Moon, a working base a few years in. Dark, lit only by its own fittings: glowing screens and amber displays set in dark grey consoles, thin white light strips, warm globe lamps, pools of teal and amber light, small red status lights. Dense, purposeful equipment built into curved walls that sweep up into the ceiling, cable runs, handrails, labels with small red characters, orange padded bunks and seats, orange and white door frames. Tidy and purposeful, not cluttered. The 360 scene is faultless.

prologue_flat.name: the player's flat in the opening

style.text: Late at night on launch night inside a small, lived-in one-room state flat of a rocket launch-site worker, on the third floor of an old concrete housing block in a Chinese harbour city. The ceiling light is switched off and the ceiling is in darkness; the room is dark and moody, lit only by small pools from its own fittings: the cold blue-white glow of an old television on a low cabinet showing a man speaking at a red podium, a warm green-shaded lamp on the table, a small warm lamp by the bed, and red and gold glow from the rally in the square coming in through the glass balcony door. Whitewashed walls with a glossy dark green painted lower band, worn reddish-brown painted floorboards, a narrow single bed with a folded quilt, a varnished wooden table with two wooden chairs, a tall varnished wooden wardrobe, a small kitchen corner with a two-ring gas stove, a kettle, a sink and shelves of bowls, a thermos flask, an enamel washbasin on a stand, a wall calendar, a framed family photograph, a red poster with Chinese characters, slippers by the bed. Photograph, tidy but lived in, deep shadows, low key, no cream padding.
style.from: the flat's painting (WORK/scene/prologue-flat/style.txt and marble/paint.json, seed 7), moved into the repo 2026-10-04

prologue_stairwell.name: the stairwell down from the flat

style.text: Night inside the enclosed concrete stair core of an old Hong Kong public housing block in 2099: switchback flights of terrazzo steps with painted steel rails, landings with flat doors behind steel security gates and red couplets, caged bulkhead lamps, meter boxes, conduit and cable bundles up the walls, whitewashed walls gone grey with a dark green gloss lower band peeling in places, a fire extinguisher, letterboxes and a notice board in the ground lobby, a steel gate to the street. Worn, damp and lived in, lit a pool at a time by the caged lamps.

expedition_camp.name: the first expedition's camp on Mars

style.text: An American private company's camp (SpaceXcitement, 2099), landed by one company ship and put up by three people, then lived in for a year; not a state base. Inflatable soft-goods domes: a woven fabric shell banded by load straps over a ring of padded tubes at the foot, quilted fabric panels between aluminium ribs inside, rigid window frames set in the fabric, a roof ring with a vent fan. Rigid parts in brushed stainless steel, anodised aluminium and carbon composite, rounded corners, smooth consumer products, flush touchscreens, few bolts showing; company and mission graphics stencilled on cargo cases. After a year: fine Mars dust in every seam and drifted against everything outside, scuffed and patched fabric, tape repairs, cables run loose, opened cargo cases turned into furniture, personal photographs and notes.
style.from: the camp's concept step (mars-build, 2026-10-07): outside K05, door dome K01, far dome K08
style.picked: coordinator's pick, owner may change (owner reviews world 1 at the end, 2026-10-07)

style.text: The first south-pole station on the Moon, built in the 2030s from real engineering of that decade and kept going 65 years later by one old caretaker: landed cylindrical modules on their own legs joined by walkway tubes, gold and silver thermal blankets faded, torn and patched, plain white painted hulls, regolith sandbags on roofs and under tubes, tall vertical solar masts, a dish on a mast, a docked six-wheeled rover. Everything matte and covered in fine grey dust, one window lit warm, low raking sun and black sky.

Low raking sun, black sky.

Lit by the magenta grow lights over the beds and the work lamps, the Moon and the black sky through the glass.

style.text: The bridge in the nose of the crew's Mars shuttle: a low, dark cockpit for a working crew, grounded and practical, worn by use, not sleek. Two chunky padded pilot seats side by side face a wide dark grey console of three screens glowing warm amber and orange, a throttle pedestal with levers between them, and angled side consoles with red-lit switches under the angled side windows; behind them a raised command spot with its own seat and a low console. Dark grey panelled walls and ceiling, heavy frame ribs between the windows and up the side walls, overhead vent and equipment boxes, a grated step between the seats. Lit low: warm amber light strips along the ceiling's edges and small orange lamps, cool cyan light panels over the windshield and a cyan bar along the console, real shadow between. The aft door is a hexagonal frame in orange-and-white panels, as through the rest of the ship.
style.from: the owner's locked ship design of 2026-10-01: his cockpit reference for the bridge's look (dark grey panelled consoles, amber screens and light strips, cyan accents, chunky seats), his cutaway reference for its layout (a raised command spot behind the pilots, the walkway aft) and his quarters reference for the ship's door frames
